tool.name: RuleTableAttributeUpdater
tool.summary: Changes attribute values with a rule table: each rule has a RULE_ID, a SQL WHERE_CLAUSE, a FIELD and a NEW_VALUE. Rules run in table order and the first matching rule wins for each feature and field. The default is a dry run that writes only a change log; APPLY_TO_COPY writes the corrected features to a new feature class. The input is never edited.

param.name: in_features
param.dialogReference: Features to correct (a layer's selection and definition query are honoured). Never edited.

param.name: rule_table
param.dialogReference: Table with the columns RULE_ID, WHERE_CLAUSE, FIELD and NEW_VALUE. Use this or Rule File.

param.name: rule_file
param.dialogReference: CSV (UTF-8) or Excel (.xlsx or .xlsm) file with RULE_ID, WHERE_CLAUSE, FIELD and NEW_VALUE in its first row. Use this or Rule Table.

param.name: rule_sheet
param.dialogReference: Worksheet of the .xlsx rule file (default: the first worksheet that is visible in Excel; a hidden sheet is read only when it is chosen here). Ignored for CSV.

param.name: mode
param.dialogReference: DRY_RUN (default): write only the change log (and rule report). APPLY_TO_COPY: also write the corrected features to Output Features.

param.name: domain_violations
param.dialogReference: REFUSE (default): stop, before anything is copied or written, when a NEW_VALUE is not in the coded-value or range domain of its field (field-level and subtype-level domains). WARN: write it anyway and warn. For a coded-value domain, NEW_VALUE is the CODE, not its description.

param.name: out_features
param.dialogReference: New feature class for APPLY_TO_COPY: a copy of the input with the rules applied. Required for APPLY_TO_COPY, ignored for DRY_RUN.

param.name: out_log
param.dialogReference: New table with one row per changed cell: RULE_ID, FEATURE_OID, FIELD, OLD_VALUE, NEW_VALUE, APPLIED, SRC_OID. Write it to a geodatabase to keep NULL distinct from empty text.

param.name: out_rule_report
param.dialogReference: Optional new table with one row per rule: RULE_ID, MATCHED, CHANGED, ALREADY_OK, SKIPPED_EARLIER_RULE, RULE_ROW, FIELD, NOTE.

param.name: cells_changed
param.dialogReference: Number of cells changed (APPLY_TO_COPY) or that would change (DRY_RUN); derived.

tool.usage:
Use it to apply a reviewed set of corrections (a default speed per road class, a standard spelling, a status for empty cells) to many features, and to keep a record of exactly what changed. Calculate Fields (multiple) also sets values where a condition is true and is the simpler choice for one or two updates on data you may edit; this tool adds rules kept as a table or file, a dry run as the default, a change log of every changed cell, a report per rule, first matching rule wins, and a corrected copy instead of an edit in place.

FIELD is matched to a field of the input by its exact name first, then by alias and name ignoring letter case, spaces, underscores, dashes and the Arabic tatweel (speed-kph finds SPEED_KPH); a text that fits two fields is refused. The change log holds the real field name. RULE_ID has 1 to 40 letters, digits, _ or -; vowel marks after a letter (the Arabic harakat) are allowed. It must be unique, letter case ignored (STRASSE and Strasse with the sharp s are two ids).

The rule table is a geodatabase table (or any table ArcGIS Pro can read) with the columns RULE_ID, WHERE_CLAUSE, FIELD and NEW_VALUE, or a CSV (UTF-8) or .xlsx file with those names in its first row (from an .xlsx file, the first sheet visible in Excel unless Rule File Sheet names another). Give either Rule Table or Rule File. Rules run in ObjectID order (table) or row order (file). A rule table layer's selection or definition query is honoured. Empty rows are ignored.

How the rules work: WHERE_CLAUSE is SQL in the dialect of the input data (for a file geodatabase, for example: RD_CLASS = 'primary' AND (LANES IS NULL OR LANES < 1)). A field name with a sign such as ':' or '-' (name:ar or speed-kph in a GeoPackage) must be written in double quotes in a WHERE clause ("name:ar" = 'x'); FIELD takes the name as it is. Every WHERE clause is evaluated against the data as it was before the run, so a rule never sees the result of an earlier rule. For a given feature and field the first rule that matches wins; later matching rules skip that cell and count it as SKIPPED_EARLIER_RULE. Different fields of one feature are independent. A rule that matches a cell that already holds NEW_VALUE changes nothing and counts it as ALREADY_OK. Running the same rules on their own output is sure to change 0 cells when no WHERE clause reads a field that another rule writes. When one does (for example R1 sets CLS to 'b' and R2 matches CLS = 'b'), the later rule does not see the new value and a second run can change more cells: the tool lists such WHERE clauses in its messages and, after APPLY_TO_COPY, runs the rules again on every feature of the copy without writing and warns with the number of cells a second run would change (cells of features this run did not change are counted apart: a shapefile copy stores NULL as 0 or as empty text (ArcGIS Pro writes one space), so a rule can match them in the copy and not in the input). Unwritten cells that a shapefile or dBASE copy stores in its own form (NULL as empty text, one space or 0) are reported in an information message, not as a difference. When the copy has new ObjectIDs (a selection, or deleted rows) and a WHERE clause names the ObjectID field, that check is skipped with a message: the same clause would select other features in the copy, so do not run such rules again on the copy as they are.

NEW_VALUE is text that is cast to the type of FIELD (String, SmallInteger, Integer, BigInteger, Single, Double). A whole number may be written 120 or 120.0; a decimal number uses a point, digits 0-9 only, and no thousands separator: 1,000 is refused and the message names both readings (1000, or 1 with a decimal comma), and in a whole-number field 1.000 is refused as ambiguous (1 or 1000). In a Single or Double field a point is always the decimal point (1.000 is 1). The token <NULL> (any letter case) sets the field to NULL. A number written with an exponent (1e3) is refused for a whole-number field; write 1000. A Double field keeps the nearest value it can store (1e-400 becomes 0, 9007199254740993 becomes 9007199254740992): the tool warns, and the change log holds the stored value (a Single field keeps the nearest float32, without a warning; 1e-50 is stored and logged as 0.0). An empty NEW_VALUE is refused, not treated as empty text, and so is one made only of spaces. Other text is written as typed, spaces included; a text that starts or ends with a space gets a warning.

Checked before anything is copied or written, and reported together with the rule id and the row (file) or ObjectID (table) of every problem: a missing or repeated RULE_ID, an empty WHERE_CLAUSE, an unknown or ambiguous FIELD, a protected field (ObjectID, geometry, GlobalID, GUID, blob, raster, XML, read-only and the usual system fields), an unsupported field type (for example Date), a NEW_VALUE that is not a valid number, is out of range for the type, is longer than a text field, or is <NULL> for a field that does not allow NULL, for APPLY_TO_COPY a FIELD whose name the output workspace would change (a GeoPackage field name:ar becomes name_ar in a file geodatabase and in a GeoPackage copy), and a WHERE clause that the data refuses. Nothing is changed or created while one of these is open. A NEW_VALUE outside the field's coded-value or range domain is refused too (Domain Violations = REFUSE, the default) or written with a warning (WARN). Field-level and subtype-level domains are both checked: a field with domains per subtype is judged for each changed feature against the domain of its own subtype, and the message names the rule, the subtype and the number of cells outside the domain. For a coded-value domain NEW_VALUE and the change log hold the code, not its description. Warnings (nothing is refused): a text NEW_VALUE such as NULL, None, <None>, NA, N/A or nan (any letter case), which is written as that text (use <NULL> to set NULL; a real code such as NA gets the warning too), a rule that edits the subtype field of the dataset, a number a Double field cannot hold exactly, a WHERE clause that reads a field another rule writes, a text NEW_VALUE with an invisible character (U+200F RIGHT-TO-LEFT MARK copied with an Arabic text: it is written as it is, so a later WHERE clause on the visible text does not find it), and an Excel number cell written into a text field (Excel keeps 007 typed as a number as 7, so the zeros are already gone; format the cell as Text, or with the number format 000, which is read as 007).

Outputs. Change Log (always): one row per changed cell, RULE_ID, FEATURE_OID (the ObjectID in the dataset that was or would be edited), FIELD, OLD_VALUE, NEW_VALUE (complete text; a NULL stays NULL), APPLIED (NO for a dry run, YES when applied) and SRC_OID (the ObjectID in the input). Rule Report (optional): one row per rule with MATCHED, CHANGED, ALREADY_OK and SKIPPED_EARLIER_RULE (MATCHED is always the sum of the other three), the rule table row, the field and a note for a rule that matched nothing or whose matches were all taken by earlier rules. The change log is enough to undo an APPLY_TO_COPY run: the OLD_VALUE of every row is the value to restore (see the tool page).

APPLY_TO_COPY copies the input (a layer's selection and definition query are honoured) to Output Features with Copy Features, so the copy has the input's schema, then writes the new values into the copy. The changes are worked out on the input, the same way as in a dry run, so a dry run and an apply run report the same changes. Copy Features may renumber ObjectIDs (for example a geopackage fid); the tool pairs the rows by ObjectID order, proves the pairing by comparing every text, number and date field and the geometry (centroid, length, area) of each row with the input before it writes anything, and stops without leaving a copy if the rows do not line up. After writing it re-reads the copy and warns if a stored value differs from the intended one (a dBASE or shapefile output rounds numbers and cuts trailing spaces); a cell the run did not write that such an output stores in its own form (NULL as empty text, one space or 0) is named in an information message instead. If anything fails after the copy was made, the unfinished copy is deleted. A joined layer cannot be applied (remove the join first). A shapefile or dBASE output cannot store NULL: a rule with <NULL> is refused there, and so is a rule for a field name longer than 10 bytes (about 5 Arabic letters) (the shapefile would cut the name); the change log must be in a geodatabase if any old or new value is NULL.

Existing outputs are replaced only when geoprocessing is allowed to overwrite outputs. An output that is the input, the rule table or another output is refused in the dialog before ArcGIS Pro can delete anything.
